heading: ### `Claim`
text:
A `Claim` has no `name`. It is identified by the FQN `<actor fqn>::<attribute name>::<claimType>` (for example `<Model>::<Actor>::email::EMAIL`); a query that selects `name` on `claims` fails with `Field 'name' in type 'ESM_Claim' is undefined`. Create one with the actor as parent and the principal's attribute as target (the actor needs a principal first; the attribute must belong to the principal TO):

```bash
judo create -t Claim --ns <Model>::<Actor> --set claimType=EMAIL --set attribute=<Model>::<PrincipalTO>.<attribute>
judo query esm Claim -s fqn,claimType
```

`claimType` is `EMAIL`, `USERNAME` or `UNDEFINED`.

heading: ### Instance Functions
text: `!container(Type)` also works as the getter of a derived relation on the contained entity, typed as the container with cardinality `0..1`: `self!container(<Parent>)`. The result can be narrowed with `!asType(<Sub>)`. `Type` must be a type that can contain `self` (a composition owner, including its supertypes or subtypes); otherwise the expression build fails with `<Type> type is not a container type of <Self type>`, also when `Type` is the type itself. A mapped transfer object relation can expose the derived relation by binding to it.

heading: ### RelationMember Rules
text:
### Range expressions on relations

- `rangeExpression` is only editable when `rangeType = DERIVED`; with `rangeType = DERIVED` a non-blank `rangeExpression` is required (EVL `DerivedRangeHasRangeExpression`). It applies to a stored entity relation and to a transient or editable mapped transfer object relation.
- `self` is allowed: `self.<relation>` and `self!container(<Type>).<path>` are valid range expressions (they build and the range is evaluated per instance), as is a type-level expression such as `<Model>::<Entity>!filter(e | ...)`.
- The server enforces the range. A value that is not in the range of the reference is rejected with `NOT_ACCEPTED_BY_RANGE`; an empty range only logs a warning.
- With `rangeType = ANY` the whole target type is the range and `rangeExpression` is read-only (the CLI rejects setting it).

heading: ### Enumeration
text: An enumeration literal is written `<Model>::<EnumType>#<LITERAL>`, for example `defaultExpression = "<Model>::<EnumType>#<LITERAL>"` on a stored attribute. Use the fully qualified type name, as for other types (see 5.2); `<EnumType>#<LITERAL>` also passes `validate` in the CLI.

heading: ### Faults and the generated exception
note: Only two fault rules exist in ESM and PSM validation: cardinality 1..1 (FaultCardinalityIsValid) and a target must be defined (OperationFaultTargetsAreDefined). A fault whose target TO is mapped to an entity is not rejected by validate (no fault-specific error in the CLI run). 'Must be unmapped' is therefore not enforced by validation; any generator-side failure was not found. Existing doc already states 1..1.

heading: ## Signed Identifiers
text: `immutable` is not an attribute of entities or transfer objects in the ESM and cannot be set in the model. It is a flag of the generated transfer operations; the ESM→PSM transformation sets it to `true` on the `_getRangeReference<Relation>` operations (relation and input-parameter ranges) and on the get-template operation, and PSM→ASM writes it as an `immutable` annotation. Instances returned by those operations are signed as immutable.

heading: ## Statements and syntax
text:
- `mutable`/`immutable` is a JCL concept, not an ESM attribute of references. Everything read from an operation's `input` is immutable, and navigating from an immutable object (including a transient reference of the input) stays immutable.
- On an immutable object, a bound operation call fails (`Cannot call operation on immutable object`), `as Type` fails (`Cannot spawn immutable objects`), `return` of it fails (`Cannot return with immutable object.`), assigning it into mutable state fails (`Invalid operation with immutable object`), and changing a collection through it fails (`Immutable selector`). Create a mutable copy with `new mutable Type(...)` to modify data.

heading: #### In TransferObjectType (unmapped)
text: An unmapped transfer object accepts only `STATIC` operations (EVL `UnmappedTransferObjectTypeHasStaticOperations`). The ESM→PSM transformation creates each as an unbound operation placed in that transfer object's own PSM equivalent (rule `CreateInPlaceUnboundOperation`); a `STATIC` operation on an entity is instead placed in the entity's default transfer object. Any unmapped transfer object can therefore carry static operations, not only a `StaticOperations` container.
note: How an actor reaches the operation (access or menu item) was not settled in source; text above states only the model/transformation facts.

heading: ### Collection Functions
text:
JQL has no union operator. To combine direct roles with roles reached through groups, navigate through the multi-valued relations or filter the target type:

```
// roles of the groups only (navigation flattens collections)
self.roleGroups.roles
// direct roles plus group roles, each role once
<Model>::Role!filter(r | self.roles!contains(r) or self.roleGroups.roles!contains(r))
```

Use the second form as the getter of a derived `effectiveRoles` relation (`0..*`).

heading: ### DataColumn
text: A derived attribute is sortable and filterable in a generated table like a stored one. The UI model marks an attribute filterable when its container is mapped, its member type is not `TRANSIENT` (a mapped attribute bound to a transient one is excluded too) and its type is string, numeric, boolean, date, timestamp, time or enumeration. The React generator makes a column sortable and filterable unless it is binary or `TRANSIENT`. A `TRANSIENT` column shows `This column is not sortable.`

heading: ### Collection Functions
text: `!count()` of an empty or missing collection is `0` (the query wraps it in `COALESCE(..., 0)`). `!sum`, `!min` and `!max` are plain SQL aggregates without a default: on an empty collection the result is `undefined` (SQL `NULL`), not `0`; item values that are `undefined` are skipped by the aggregate. Use `!isDefined()` or a conditional to supply a default, for example `self.items!sum(i | i.points)!isDefined() ? self.items!sum(i | i.points) : 0`.
note: Empty-collection result derived from the generated SQL (no COALESCE for SUM); not observed with a running database. The conditional example expression was not run.

heading: #### RelationKind Behaviour
### Default Values on Type Creation
text:
A new model from the standard template contains these string types (limits are model data, not platform constants; the platform enforces `maxLength` with `MAX_LENGTH_VALIDATION_FAILED`):

| Type | `maxLength` | `regExp` |
|------|-------------|----------|
| `String` | 255 | - |
| `Phone` | 20 | - |
| `Text` | 250 | - |
| `URL` | 1024 | - |
| `Email` | 255 | `^[_A-Za-z0-9-\\+]+(\\.[_A-Za-z0-9-]+)*@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(\\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)*(\\.[A-Za-z]{2,})$` |
| `LowerCaseString` | 127 | `^[a-z]*$` |

Numeric types: `Integer` precision 9 / scale 0, `Long` 18 / 0, `Double` 15 / 4, `Float` 7 / 4.

heading: ### VisualElement
text: `customImplementation = true` is the marker that turns any visual element (button, table column, widget, placeholder) into a custom implementation. It is copied to the UI model, and the generator exposes the element as an extension point instead of generating its content: a column is wrapped by `<column>ColumnCustomizer` when one is registered; other elements render through a proxy that looks up a registered component (see the frontend advanced patterns).
